messages:
Jordan P: Heads-up, canary rollout 0f3a2b0 for runtime kernel-autoselect shows a sharp p95 streaming latency bump on prod-r1 starting ~08:42 UTC. Investigating.
Samira K: saw that spike on dashboards, p95 up ~150ms, p99 ~400ms. Seems correlated with streams that trigger tool-calls. :thinking:
Alex B: Any deploys around then besides kernel change? I saw a framing_v2 push earlier today.
Jordan P: framing_v2 + kernel-autoselect landed together in that rollout. I suspect an interaction. CI perf ran green but only unit-level.
Maya R: CI perf job actually failed briefly earlier — QA Bot auto-muted it. QA Bot: CI Perf Job #874 failed latency threshold (p95 +11%).
Samira K: I'm starting a lightweight bisect across commits. If kernel-autoselect picks different kernels when batch sizes shrink, it can regress small-write streaming.
Alex B: Reproduced locally with a synthetic fanout test: with framing_v2 enabled, many tiny frames cause kernel choice to prefer kernel-A which has worse per-token overhead.
Jordan P: Profiling dump (sampled stacks) attached: 
```
# flame: topsomestack
runtime::serialize_frame
kernel_A::init
kv_cache::lookup (hot)
```
Seems serialization + kernel_A init cost.
Maya R: KV cache warmup traces show a lot of cross-shard RPCs during first 30s after canary. That could amplify per-request tail.
Alex B: Suggest two options: 1) revert framing_v2, or 2) force kernel-autoselect to prefer low-latency kernels for small sequences and defer kernel_A for longer batches. We can also add a microcache to avoid repeated shard lookups.
Jordan P: Can we hit quick feature-flag to force kernel=fast-path on canary? How invasive?
Samira K: It's a runtime flag; low-risk. I'll flip on canary and rerun perf harness. Command: `./runtime_ctl set-flag canary:kernel_pref=fast-path`
DevInfra Bot: rollflag applied to canary hosts: canary:kernel_pref=fast-path (ID: roll-6421)
Jordan P: After flag: p95 dropped back ~110ms, p99 still high but improved. Tool-call serialization still shows extra copies.
Alex B: Found a double-copy inside the toolcall wrapper in framing_v2: `serde::to_bytes` then `write_frame` does another copy. Patch incoming to avoid the second allocation.
Maya R: QA will run the perf harness once Alex's patch is in. If that fixes toolcall overhead, we can rollforward with kernel_pref stay.
Samira K: Also queued a CI perf job with real streaming workload on staging. QA Bot: CI Perf Job #875 queued.
Jordan P: Decision: hold global rollout. Continue canary with kernel_pref fast-path + Alex's patch. If CI875 passes and p99 stabilizes, schedule rollforward. If not, prepare revert for framing_v2.
Alex B: sending PR now: `PR #4127` — avoids second copy, adds a microbenchmark. cc @Samira K
Maya R: thx. I'll monitor. :thumbsup:
Samira K: bisection notes: suspected commits: framing_v2 (sha 0f3a2b0), kernel-autoselect tweaks (sha 7c9d1f4). Root cause appears to be composition of framing change + kernel selection heuristics.
Jordan P: Good triage. Keep thread updated. If anyone sees a user-facing error spike, ping on-call.
QA Bot: CI Perf Job #875 passed perf thresholds (p95 within 2% of baseline).
